commit.message:
8394180: Use the local execution engine in MultipleDocumentationTest

MultipleDocumentationTest builds its JShell instances with the bare
default engine chain (failover: 0(jdi:hostname), 1(jdi:launch), 2(jdi)),
where every JDI variant must start the remote agent VM within the
fixed 5000 ms default timeout (JdiExecutionControlProvider.
DEFAULT_TIMEOUT). On slow machines the agent VM start-up to JDWP
handshake can exceed this budget, and when all three variants miss
it the JShell construction itself fails:

  IllegalStateException: Launching JShell execution engine threw:
  FailOverExecutionControlProvider: FAILED: 0:jdi:hostname(127.0.0.1) --
    ... TransportTimeoutException: timeout waiting for connection
    @ com.sun.jdi.SocketListen {timeout=5000, ...}
  FAILED: 1:jdi:launch(true) -- ... TimeoutException
  FAILED: 2:jdi -- ... TransportTimeoutException

This is the same failure mode as JDK-8300202, which was reported for
CompletionSuggestionTest and closed as a duplicate of JDK-8293000.
The test only exercises SourceCodeAnalysis documentation and never
evaluates a snippet, so the execution engine is incidental: switch
the builders to the in-process local engine, as JDK-8293000 did for
the analysis-only jshell tests (ClassMembersTest,
CompletionSuggestionTest, ...). This removes the remote start-up from
the critical path entirely and makes the test deterministic on slow
machines.

Test-only change; no product code touched.
